Cc: Ops Team <ops@fastcart.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FastCart alert: sharp latency & errors from reserved pool (prod)

Hi Soojin —

We started seeing elevated latencies and a 5% 5xx error rate across our checkout model from 08:50 PT. This is for traffic routed to the Redwood dedicated pool we reserved (FC-Standard-1). Throughput is dropping below the committed 1200 reqs/min and requests are queuing. Our SREs are seeing KV-cache misses spike and token latencies double.

Can you confirm whether the dedicated pool is experiencing saturation or whether traffic was misrouted to a lower-tier variant? This is impacting conversion on checkout. We have a renewal review next week and need the service to stabilize.

Attached a short perf dump and a screenshot of the SLO dashboard.

—Samira

Subject: Re: FastCart alert: sharp latency & errors from reserved pool (prod)

FYI — quick triage notes (between 09:00–10:00 PT):

1) Symptoms observed
- Dedicated pool FC-Standard-1 GPU p95 token latency jumped from ~18ms to ~54ms; total request RTT p95 from ~220ms -> ~880ms.
- 5xx rate climbed to 4.8% (model OOM/timeout/retry cascade).
- Batching queue depth rose sharply; batch sizes stayed within expected ranges, but backlog increased due to slower kernel execution.

2) Initial root cause hypothesis
- We’re seeing a regression in one of the low-level kernels (attention kernel path) for quantized variants on the 80GB nodes after a recent kernel auto-update rolled to the fleet at 08:30 PT. The update affected ~3 host images in the FC-Standard-1 pool.

3) Immediate actions taken
- Rolled back kernel patch on 3 impacted hosts (partial containment) — this brought down p95 token latency from 54ms -> 30ms on those hosts.
- Enabled reserved burst capacity (non-committed GPUs) and rebalanced FastCart slices onto healthy hosts to reduce queueing.
- Triggered an emergency canary (slow draining of traffic off impacted hosts).

4) Ask / next steps
- Need an exec bridge to request temporary priority capacity and to approve a one-time credit for FastCart while we complete verification (Laura/Soojin to handle comms).
- Dev team (Dev Patel) to validate that rollback is safe and produce a short RCA for the kernel update pipeline.

I’ll monitor telemetry and post an update in 30–45 minutes.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime

- We will provide a short evidence package (kernel patch IDs, timing, perf logs, and SLO charts) and a proposed one-time billing credit to FastCart for the incident window.
